title: Scientists Break 3 World Records With Giant Atoms Built for Quantum Computing
key_facts: Stuttgart 5th Institute of Physics set three records for circular Rydberg atoms
Circular state lasted 11 ms, over 20 times longer than comparable free-space states
Atoms held in an optical tweezer for 133 ms
Orbits about 1.1 micrometres, about 10,000 times ordinary atoms
Done at room temperature with transparent conductive plates, no liquid helium
Authors say stability improved by a factor of 20; article says it is not yet a complete quantum computer
quote_evidence: We achieved these record results at room temperature without the costly liquid helium cooling previously required
the records themselves are advances in the underlying technology rather than a demonstration of a complete quantum computer
why_it_matters_hint: Longer-lived atoms for neutral-atom quantum simulators.
notes: Exact publication date of the paper not stated in the text.
